issues.failure_explanation: The theorem includes every t>0, but the proof assumes t>h and its decomposition requires the first interval [0,h] and the last interval [tau_t^h-h,t] to form appropriate boundary pieces. For h<t<2h, tau_t^h-h=0, so these pieces overlap, while the intervening integrals have reversed endpoints; for t<=h the first integral extends beyond t. Thus the displayed decomposition is not valid in the omitted small-time regime.

issues.failure_explanation: Conditioning the original scheme contribution on X^h_{tau_s^h}=z and U_{tau_s^h/h}=r does not produce the displayed kernel p_alpha(t-s,y-z). By the scheme dynamics and the stable semigroup it produces a gradient at time t-tau_s^h and shifted argument y-z-b(r,z)(s-tau_s^h). Both the within-step drift and noise evolution have been discarded, so Delta_62 is not an upper bound or representation of the scheme part of Delta_6.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recondition the scheme term correctly, retain the kernel with time t-tau_s^h and its drift shift, and prove a last-step cancellation estimate for that expression using the spatial Hölder bounds and stable-kernel sensitivities.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate maj-D6-mainthm, and hence the final density-error bound, lacks a valid treatment of the Euler contribution over the last time steps.
issues.title: The last-step scheme term is replaced by a different integral
issues.why_classification: The intended tools are present, but the missing estimate is a contained nontrivial argument rather than a typographical or routine algebraic correction.

issues.failure_explanation: The remaining term Delta_3 in the original decomposition contains p_alpha(t-s), but after collecting the estimates it is silently replaced by p_alpha(t-tau_s^h), and its integration range is also enlarged. No identity or error estimate justifies this replacement. Consequently the subsequent convolution inequality and discrete Gronwall step are not applied to the actual residual term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the original t-s kernel, bound it by f(tau_s^h)(t-s)^{-1/alpha}, and justify comparison of the resulting proxy convolution at total time tau_s^h+t-s with the proxy at time t; alternatively, explicitly estimate the error caused by changing t-s to t-tau_s^h.
issues.overall_effect: The closing Gronwall argument does not bound the Delta_3 appearing in the exact error decomposition, leaving Theorem thm-main unproved.
issues.title: The Gronwall term changes the heat-kernel time argument
issues.why_classification: Away from the separately handled small-time regime, the two total times differ by at most h and are comparable, so a short local modification of the convolution estimate can retain the same Volterra bound and rate.
